en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah informed us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, the Ansar are my close confidants and my trusted repository; and indeed people will increase while they will decrease, so accept the good from those who do good among them, and overlook the faults of those who do wrong among them.'

Yahya ibn Habib narrated it to me: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kuraib narrated to us; they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us; both of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us from Ghundar; Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: A woman from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) met with her in private and said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you are indeed the most beloved of people to me,' three times.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to me from Ibn 'Ulayyah—and the wording is Zuhayr's: Isma'il narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz—who is Ibn Suhayb—from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw children and women returning from a wedding banquet, so the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood up straight and said: 'O Allah, you are among the most beloved of people to me! O Allah, you are among the most beloved of people to me!'—meaning the Ansar.

Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi narrated to me: 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Ikrimah—who is Ibn 'Ammar—narrated to us: Ishaq—who is Ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah—narrated to us that Anas narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) prayed for forgiveness for the Ansar. He said: And I think he said: 'and for the offspring of the Ansar and for the freed slaves of the Ansar'; I have no doubt about it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; they said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'O Allah, forgive the Ansar, and the children of the Ansar, and the children's children of the Ansar.' And Yahya ibn Habib narrated it to me: Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's; they said: Sufyan informed us, from 'Amr, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: Concerning us was revealed: {When two parties among you were about to lose courage, but Allah was their ally}—Banu Salimah and Banu Harithah. And we would not have liked that it had not been revealed, on account of the word of Allah, the Exalted and Glorious: {and Allah was their ally}.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from 'A'idh ibn 'Amr, that Abu Sufyan came upon Salman, Suhayb, and Bilal in a group of people, and they said: 'By Allah, the swords of Allah did not take their full due from the neck of the enemy of Allah!' He said: Thereupon Abu Bakr said: 'Do you say this to the elder of Quraysh and their master?' So he went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed him. He said: 'O Abu Bakr, perhaps you angered them? If you have angered them, you have indeed angered your Lord!' So Abu Bakr came to them and said: 'O my brothers, did I anger you?' They said: 'No, may Allah forgive you, O brother!'
